captions_note: the wall is the caption: the row over the head says every word as it is spoken
in_a_reel: the buyer's style wins: set the wall typeface, INK and ACCENT from the reel's caption style before building (effects/INDEX.md, "Restyling an effect's own words")
set IN_FRAME to the frame of the first wall word, a few frames after the slot starts, so the slot's first frame is the plain room
set OUT_FRAME a few frames before the slot ends (the room has to be back), unless the slot ends on a cut or at the end of the reel
the speaker sits on or behind furniture: draw its top edge in KEEP, or the speaker floats on the wall
steps: run prep.py      # measure the speaker, then LOOK at work/measure.jpg (yellow line on top of the speaker's head, blue tint = everywhere the speaker goes)
run onsets.py -v      # 3. word frames from the audio; read the per-frame loudness strip for every wall word
edit the CLIP block in build.py: PHRASES always, KEEP when the speaker sits on or behind something.
run build.py SAFE=1      # build with the guide on, lint, look at snapshots (one per swap, one at the end); read its row table and any "!!" lines
hf snapshot --at <times in seconds, comma separated>
